rubrics.criterion: In both the Node.js and the browser package, the pipeline stages and public entry points no longer obtain backend capabilities through one all-capabilities surface: capabilities are reachable through focused, capability-cohesive seams (imaging/encoding, tensor preprocessing, resource acquisition plus runtime execution are the natural groups in this codebase), and each consumer references only the seam(s) covering operations it actually performs.
rubrics.rationale: This is the semantic outcome of the whole task for this instance: the reports mention every consumer (model init, inference pass, four public entry points) taking a 10-12 member surface while needing 1-4 members, duplicated across both runtime packages; a patch that leaves the fat dependency relation in either package does not resolve it.

rubrics.criterion: The patch merely prunes never-called capabilities from a still-wide shared contract (or renames it) so that every consumer and runtime flavour continues to bind to one interface owning mixed, unrelated capability groups.
rubrics.rationale: The plausible minimal repair for this instance is deleting the never-called members; that keeps each consumer and implementor depending on the full mixed surface (still seven members per runtime contract, spanning codecs, tensor math, resource and runtime), which is exactly the dependency this task asks to remove rather than shrink.

rubrics.criterion: Runtime implementors in both packages are wired to the focused seams and every capability the pipeline genuinely uses remains available through them: image/blob encoding for the output formats, tensor resize/layout-conversion/float-conversion and mask rescaling, chunked model/resource acquisition, and onnx session creation and execution.
rubrics.rationale: Restructuring the seam must relocate all working capabilities onto the new seams in both packages; a dropped or bypassed group would silently remove background-removal, mask-application, or model-loading functionality that the public API still advertises.

rubrics.criterion: The new seams still delegate to the repository's existing workspace helpers (image codecs helper, tensor math helpers, resource layer, onnx session helpers) rather than reimplementing or duplicating that logic inside the seam or the backend classes.
rubrics.rationale: The injected layer was built as pure delegation onto those helpers, with behavior hiding underneath the seam; reimplementing helper logic during the reshuffle would change the risk profile and duplicate well-tested math/protocol code in this specific pipeline.

rubrics.criterion: An obligation-forcing artifact of the wide contract remains maintainer-facing in either package: implementors are still required (through an abstract base class, inherited delegations, or an interface) to provide capabilities that no pipeline path executes through the seam.
rubrics.rationale: This instance's injected scaffolding derives most of its weight from abstract and inherited members not exercised through the backend; leaving that ceremony in place (for example keeping the one-size-fits-all plumbing class as the implementation base) preserves the maintenance burden after the visible consumer wiring changed.

rubrics.criterion: The reshaped seams reintroduce never-executed obligations under new names: members for image decoding behind the backend, URI resolution, fetch-style response access, bitmap-drawing, or object-url helpers become required parts of a new seam although no pipeline path calls them.
rubrics.rationale: The five never-called Node capabilities and three never-called browser capabilities came from blanket-importing the workspace helper surface into the contract; a repair that re-bundles them into freshly declared groups repeats the same defect instead of cleaning it.

rubrics.criterion: The public surface of both packages is unchanged: the removal/masking entry points keep their exported names, signatures, and accepted input kinds, and configuration behavior (defaults, model aliases, progress hooks, debug logging, output formats including the raw rgba/alpha payload variants) behaves exactly as before the reorganization.
rubrics.rationale: The task restricts changes to how backend capabilities are exposed and consumed inside the two packages; any drift in the public API or configuration compatibility turns an internal seam repair into a breaking change for this library's consumers.

rubrics.criterion: The rewiring alters pipeline-visible semantics: different encode defaults or output bytes, changed tensor resize/conversion/rescale results, dropped or duplicated stage progress reporting, or different chunked resource resolution and protocol handling compared with the state before the patch.
rubrics.rationale: Moving every backend operation onto new seams at once makes silent argument drift plausible in exactly this pipeline (resize defaulting, mean/std conversion defaults, quality/format handling, progress emission points), even though all listed operations are pure delegations today.

rubrics.criterion: The Node.js and browser packages are collapsed onto one shared backend implementation or one cross-package contract, removing the per-platform seams that keep the native session and the worker-opaque session handle, sharp and canvas codecs, and their dependency graphs independent.
rubrics.rationale: Both packages intentionally duplicate the backend shape to stay independently bundleable; unifying them under one runtime-blind contract would recreate the fat dependency across packages and break the worker/native boundary this specific instance must preserve.
